title: Tape
description: Ask Me Why on a long ribbon of dark brown oxide tape with a satin sheen, the song's spectrogram faintly embossed into the coating, running out of a matte graphite reel-to-reel deck that only peeks in from the left edge of the page. Grab the tape or rock the reel and the song plays under your hand at the speed you pull, backwards too, while the reel turns with it and the motor drags it back to pitch.
intent: A varispeed tape you can hold, running out of a real tape machine at the edge of the page, where the paper, the printed words, the reel and the sound all move with your hand.

changelog.summary:
Audio fix: the tape head was steered with the main thread AudioContext.currentTime, which only advances once per audio callback, so a 30/s position servo turned that jitter into 2 to 11 percent pitch wobble at frame rate even at steady 1x; steering now maps the rAF timestamp onto the audio clock through getOutputTimestamp with a smoothed offset, and steady playback holds pitch within 0.1 percent.
Audio fix: hand scratches no longer buzz at the pointer rate; every coalesced pointer sample is recorded with its own timestamp, the audio follows the hand path 24ms behind with a windowed slope, and roughness dropped about tenfold in simulation.
Audio fix: the transport no longer loses time on slow frames (it substeps the real interval up to 250ms), so dropped frames stop dragging the pitch.
Tape head DSP rebuilt as a varispeed with mass: separate held and motor followers, a gentle position trim, equal-power 30ms crossfades instead of fade-to-silence jumps, a DC blocker for reversal thumps, a soft tape saturation instead of hard clipping, and output level that falls with speed like a real playback head.
Visual audio lag compensation removed; the worklet now leads by the measured output latency instead, so picture and sound line up without delaying the paper.
New: a reel-to-reel deck drawn under the strip, its play head right below the blue playhead, with brushed aluminium plate, two NAB reels whose oxide packs grow and shrink with tape position, three heads, capstan, pinch roller and tension arms.
Reels turn clockwise forward and back in reverse at the true rate for their pack radius, the pinch roller turns with the tape, spokes motion-blur at shuttle speed, and the tension arms swing with tape strain; the tape path re-threads as the packs change.
New: grab either reel and rock it to scrub, the way engineers find an edit point; it feeds the same hold, fling and motor physics as the strip.
The time and speed readouts moved into the deck as its counter window and varispeed readout; Worn tape now also adds a little speed-dependent hiss.
Lyric lane, ink print, smear, wear, shuttle chips, keyboard, word seeking and cast chips are unchanged.
Scratch fix: held audio no longer runs ahead of the hand. The worklet now extrapolates a held target by at most one frame past its own measured message delay, never past the newest pointer sample (the transport sends how far the known hand path reaches and the worklet clamps to it), the hand slope is centred instead of trailing, and the held servo is retuned to stiffness 8, trim 3 and a 4ms follower. In an offline run of the real DSP a 3x pull stopped dead now overshoots 13ms instead of 193ms (565ms at 150ms latency) with a -0.1x tail instead of a -3.2x chirp, a 4Hz wiggle is 6 percent wide instead of 138 to 420 percent, there are no crossfade jumps at any latency, and steady pulls hold pitch within 0.2 percent.
Hand delay raised from 24 to 32ms so a whole frame of real hand path is always known ahead of the audio, which keeps 60Hz trackpads and 30fps frames from pinching the pitch at every frame boundary.
Seek fix: arrow keys and word taps run the head with no latency lead, stiffness 20 and trim 4, so the audio lands where the picture lands (28ms, the transport's own settle) instead of 150 to 750ms past it, with no jumps up to 60ms latency.
Releasing the tape or finishing a seek now hands the held delay over to the motor as a lag that is spent inside the following speed glide (and at 1 percent pitch at most otherwise), so a fling no longer chirps sharp to catch up with the picture.
A main thread stall longer than 300ms now keeps the motor at its last speed instead of dragging the head down an octave.
Levels: the loop is peak normalised to -1 dBFS and the head outputs at 0.76, so 1x peaks sit below the saturation knee; tape saturation now only bends shuttle and scratch peaks.
Deck performance: the brushed plate, screws, head block, counter window and reel wells are one static SVG layer; packs, tape path, arms, posts and pinch roller are a thin threading layer; each reel's spokes, hub and motion blur ring are their own SVG layers turned and faded with CSS transform and opacity on the compositor, as is the pinch roller mark. The eight blurred filter shadows are now pre-blurred radial gradient ellipses.
The brushed metal pattern covers the full 560x256 plate, so the streaks no longer repeat in four horizontal bands.
Spoke motion blur and the pinch mark fade key off angular speed in rad/s (6 to 25 for spokes) with frame-time based easing, so they look the same at 60 and 120Hz and stop flickering at shuttle speed.
Reel grips use touch-action pan-y: a horizontal turn or a 160ms hold claims a reel, and a vertical swipe on the deck scrolls the page.
Reel hover: the accent ring is gone; a soft highlight brightens across the metal flange on hover and while that reel is held.
On phones the counter and speed readouts are counter-scaled against the deck's transform, so they render at 13 and 14px instead of 8 to 12px.

The tape deck moved from the middle of the page to the left edge and only peeks in: 128px of it on desktop and 80px on phones, the rest off canvas, so all you see is the plate edge, two corner screws and the right half of one reel with its oxide pack.
The deck now sits over the left end of the strip, 24px taller than the strip above and below on desktop and 16px on phones, so the printed tape reads as running out from under it across the page instead of passing over a machine underneath.
The visible reel still turns with the tape at the true rate for its pack, clockwise forward and back in reverse, with the same spoke motion blur, hover highlight and rock-to-scrub grip; the second reel is off canvas, so its unreachable grip was removed.
The blue playhead is no longer pinned to the deck play head: it sits at 38 percent of the width and at least 64px clear of the deck, and overhangs the strip by 12px at both ends again instead of reaching down into the deck.
The time and speed readouts left the hidden counter window and are back under the playhead below the strip at their original sizes, which also drops the phone counter-scaling.
On load the deck slides 40px in from the left edge with a fade; under reduced motion it is simply there.
The intro now says rock the reel, since only one reel is visible.
Audio, transport, lyric lane, ink print, smear, wear, shuttle chips and keyboard are unchanged.

The strip is now magnetic tape instead of paper: a ribbon of dark brown oxide with a slightly lit upper half falling into shade below, lighter slit edges top and bottom that curl up and catch the light, faint longitudinal coating streaks and a fine oxide grain that travel with the tape.
A soft satin sheen runs along the tape in a fixed light pool; its crest and gloss follow a slow ripple printed in the tape itself, so the highlight undulates as the tape moves and brightens and tightens where you stretch the tape at the head.
The spectrogram is no longer a bright ink chart: it is a low contrast warmer tone in the oxide with a faint emboss lit from above, which glints where it passes through the sheen; it still records out from the playhead on load and motion blurs at shuttle speed.
Worn tape now scrapes thin lighter lines along the length, makes the print blotchy and dulls the sheen.
The second ticks along the bottom are small lighter marks in the oxide, longer every five seconds.
Before audio loads the blank tape shows with a soft satin glint sweeping across it, and without WebGL the strip falls back to a CSS oxide gradient with lit edges.
The lyrics lane on top of the tape is gone, along with tap a word to seek and its smear blur; the lyric timing is still fetched only to switch the singer faces in the track chip.
The deck is dark matte graphite instead of bright brushed aluminium: plate, reel flange, hub, screws and heads were all stepped down to low contrast greys, the brushing is barely there, the white rim and screw highlights dropped from 70 to 90 percent to 5 to 7, and the reel sheen from 45 to 6 percent.
The deck's oxide pack and tape path now match the strip's brown, the reel label is a muted warm grey, and the reel hover highlight sits on the visible right half of the reel at 15 percent so it still reads without glare.
Audio, transport, playhead, readouts, reel physics, shuttle chips and keyboard are unchanged.
